newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA CURACAO REFINERY MAINTENANCE DUE IN SEPT.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA CURACAO REFINERY MAINTENANCE DUE IN SEPT.

text.p: The 310,000 barrel per day (bpd) Curacao oil refinery operated by Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) is now expected to shut its 130,000 bpd crude distillation unit in the first week of September for four weeks' maintenance, a senior refinery official said on Monday.
The maintenance was delayed from early August by a fire which disabled the main 180,000 bpd distillation tower on July 31.
"In September we are planning to shut down distiller number two for its normal revision," he said.
He said the average crude throughput for the refinery in August would be about 120,000 bpd, versus a normal 185,000 bpd.
He expected to process 170,000 bpd during the last few days of the month, when the damaged crude unit should be partially returned to service.
During the maintenance he expected to run 160,000 bpd, 125,000 bpd in the damaged unit and 35,000 bpd in a thermal cracker used as a heavy crude distiller.
Complete repairs of the damaged crude distiller would take another eight weeks, he added.
